en: *The Scripture of Laozi Converting the Barbarians*, Scroll One, Part One. [Fragmentary text] ... ceasing. If one opens it, it is concise...
at the beginning of this, I wish to write it down, yet it is not with a brush...

The substance of his body was formless and beyond comparison; he drifted beyond all limits, sometimes sinking and sometimes [emerging]. His majestic brilliance eclipsed all else, coming to rest like an echo; his traces vanished like clouds dispersing. To compare his catching of the fish to the Way is insufficient to praise it; there is no depth of pity [in such a comparison]. He served as the Archivist for King Zhou for nine hundred years. His golden body remained [intact], his teeth were like jade, and his forehead was like silver. His features possessed the marks of the dragon and the rhinoceros; his ears rose above his crown, his brow was like the sun and moon, his nose had two pillars, and the center of his face was perfectly filled. His feet tread upon the "two fives" (the earth), and his hands held the "ten patterns" (the heavens). At the limit of the Infinite, he spoke of returning to Kunlun and transforming within the Hu lands. Later, he went to Jibin and subsequently to India, whereupon he finally passed away. His writings remain for future generations, eternal and never to fade.
Preface to the Scripture on Laozi’s Ascension to the West and His Conversion of the Barbarians.
First, at that time, the Most High Lord Lao, during the year of the Jia-Gengshen cycle of King Tang of the Yin dynasty, in the month of Jianwu (the seventh lunar month).
From the realm of the eternal Way,
he mounts clouds of the three vital energies (*trivṛt-prāṇa*) and rides the essence of the sun, descending upon the nine luminaries.
He entered the mouth of the Jade Woman’s profound and wondrous womb;
there he took conception as a human being and was born at Māyā on the fifteenth day of the second month of the Gengchen year.
Nine dragons spouted water to wash his form,
which transformed into nine wells.
At that time, the Old Lord’s beard and hair were white as snow.
As soon as he stepped forward,
lotus flowers sprang up with every step,
continuing all the way to the ninth.
With his left hand pointing to heaven and his right hand pointing to the earth,
he addressed the people, saying:
In the heavens above and on the earth below,
I alone am the most honored.
I shall proclaim and spread the unsurpassed Dharma.
Universally deliver all sentient beings, both moving and stationary;
pervade the ten directions and the dark realms of hell;
and deliver all those who are destined for liberation but have not yet been delivered.
He appeared and vanished among the people,
serving as a national preceptor and model;
his rank reached that of the Great Ultimate (Taiji).
The supreme immortal deity;
at that time, divine garments appeared spontaneously upon his body,
and divine incense filled the chamber.
The sun’s radiance shone with double brilliance on the ninth day of the month;
his height was nine chi.
The multitude were all astonished and deliberated,
considering him a sage who had been born with the appearance of an old man.
Therefore, he was titled "Laozi.
From within the void, a celestial deity praised his ten epithets.
As for what are called the ten [titles]: the Most High Lord Lao;

the Perfectly Divine One of Unsurpassed Wisdom; the Teacher of Emperors; the Great Man; the Honored Great Immortal; the Father of Gods and Humans; the Unconditioned Superior Person; the Benevolent One of Great Compassion; the Celestial Worthy of Original Commencement; and the Lord Lao who followed these.
He concentrated his spirit while blending in with the mundane,
teaching and transforming devas and humans,
and expounding both the methods for governing the self and those for governing the external world.
After more than one hundred years,
the Way of the King was about to decline;
he began to slaughter the worthy and the good.
He wronged and harmed countless people;
though loyal ministers earnestly remonstrated,
he was ultimately executed and his clan exterminated.
A great flood descended from heaven,
yet he remained entirely without realization;
such was the state of affairs for many years.
It was extinguished by the Zhou.
During the time of King Kang,
the year was Jiazi.
He was also like a secular official,
concealing his traces and hiding his name as a scribe beneath the pillar.
The Master assisted the King until the year of his passing,
which was the year of Gui-chou.
He then set out toward the west,
passed through the Hangu Pass,
and was granted the five thousand chapters and verses of the Dao De Jing.
He also taught the *Miaozhen* (Wondrous Truth), *Xisheng* (Ascending to the West), and other scriptures,

as well as the supreme methods of the *Taiqing* (Great Clarity), the true texts of the Three Caverns (*Sandong*), the *Lingbao* talismans and diagrams, and the methods of the *Taixuan* (Great Mystery),
instructing him to propagate these teachings.
The most refined and benevolent one ascended as an immortal,
ensuring that his legacy would never be severed;
he then immediately crossed westward.
Having traversed the shifting sands,
they arrived at the city of Vima in the kingdom of Khotan.
At that time, the Old Lord raised the Tathāgata’s staff.

He summoned his attendants, and in an instant there appeared Chisongzi, Zhonghuang Zhangren, Yuanshi Tianwang, Taiyi Yuanjun, the Six Ding Jade Maidens, the Deity Lords of the Eight Trigrams, as well as the Lords of the Dragon and Tiger, the Gongcao Messengers, the Golden-vehicle Youth, the Radiant-light Youth, the Deities of the Heaven, Earth, Water, and Space Offices; the Deities of the Sun, Moon, Mountains, Seas, Yin, Yang, Wood, Fire, Metal, and Earth Offices; the various divine lords of the Five Peaks and Four Continents; the Heavenly Lances and Martial Spirits, the Youlu Generals, the Flying Heavenly Kings, and the Immortals and Jade Maidens.
A multitude of more than one hundred thousand beings,
riding upon clouds and dragons,
arrived floating through the air.
Thereupon, the Old Lord dwelt within the Jade Canopy,
seated upon a throne of seven precious gems,
while burning incense of a hundred blends.
Various named flowers were scattered,
celestial music was performed,
and the worthies and sages of the various heavens surrounded him on all sides.
Furthermore, by means of his supernatural powers, he summoned the various kings of the Hu;
regardless of distance,
all the people assembled.
The King of Khotan, up to and including the Kings of Jūqān, Kapardha, Gomitra, the Great Yuezhi,
Tukhāra, Kumī, Khāsya, Bākhāna, Kuvata, Yatā, and Uraśā.
King Shilanfu Yan, King Hushi Jian, King Dulejian, the King of Jibin, King Hedalozhi,
the King of Persia, the King of Shule, the King of Suye,
the King of Kucha, the King of Bolor, the King of the Great Tazig, and the King of Zhini.
The King of Bamiyan, the King of Shumana, the King of Hengmei, the King of Juyue, the King of Cao’gu,
the King of Tanling, the King of Gaochang, the King of Yanqi, the King of Gongyue,
the King of Shi, the King of Suni, the King of Kang, the King of Shi, and the King of Mi.
The King of [ ], the King of Simhapura, the King of Cao, the King of He, the Kings of Greater and Lesser An,
the King of Mu, the King of Uṇaga, the King of Xunwu, the King of Huoxin,
the Queen of the Western Regions, the King of Daqin (the Great Qin), the King of Śrāvastī, and the King of Pāṭaliputra.
The King of Aṭakā, the King of Tiṇahūka, the King of Kāmala, the King of Gandhāra,
the King of Uddiyāna, the King of Kaśmīra, the King of Karaka,
the King of Bhūraka, the King of Nepāla, the King of Ṭaṭṭa, the King of Siṃhala, and the King of Kuśinagara.
The King of Rāḍha, the King of Vaiśālī, the King of Kāpila, the King of Śrāvastī, the King of Campā,
the King of Samataṭa, the King of Oḍra, the King of Sūrpāraka,
the King of Sindhu, the King of Oḍiviśa, the King of Pāṭaliputra, and the King of Śvapaca.
King Śakaṭi, King Māndhātṛ, King Nīpālaka, King Vaidiya, King Śami,
King Kharjūra, King Khañju, King Dhārādhara, King Laṅkāla,
and the kings of the five regions of India.
Thus, there were more than eighty such kings,
along with their queens and consorts,
as well as their retinues.
They surrounded him on all sides,
all coming to listen to the Dharma.
At that time, the Old Lord addressed the various kings.
Your hearts are poisonous;
you delight in committing acts of slaughter and consume nothing but flesh and blood.
"You have taken the lives of many beings.
I shall now recite for you the Yakṣa Sūtra,
so that you may cease eating meat and eat only parched barley flour."
Do not commit slaughter.
If you are unable to refrain from it,
use the flesh of animals that have died of natural causes.
The Hu people are stubborn and perverse;
they do not recognize kinship or distance,
caring only for greed and lust.
First, they lack gratitude and righteousness;
their hair and beards are matted and curled,
making even basic grooming and cleansing extremely difficult.
Since their nature is foul and their bodies are mostly filthy,
if one were to cause them to cultivate the Way...
Because they are practitioners who act out of afflictions,
I have caused them all to shave off their hair and beards;
let them wear felt and fur garments according to their original secular customs.
I shall teach you the Minor Path,
enabling you to practice and study gradually while concurrently upholding the prohibitive precepts.
Having practiced compassion to some extent,
one must always perform repentance on the fifteenth day of every month.
Furthermore, by means of his supernormal powers, he manifested the form of a transformation Buddha,
soaring through the air with a body sixteen feet tall.
Its body is golden in color;
its face always faces east,
demonstrating that it does not forget its origin.
It is because of my coming from the East that this phenomenon has been manifested,
so that those who see it may give rise to a mind of kindness and compassion.
You kings, all of you shall pay homage with your faces turned toward my single image,
while attending to affairs of state facing east.
Before long, they passed Mount Congling;
within it was a deep pool.
A venomous dragon dwelt there.
Five hundred merchants stayed overnight on the shore of the pond.
They were destroyed by the dragon,
so that not a single one remained.
I have left behind for them this royal decree from King Kapphina of that kingdom to be transmitted to you.
As he proceeded to the pond to perform the ritual,
the Dragon King became terrified and transformed himself into a human being.
He apologized to the king and requested to be moved to another residence,
so that he would no longer further harm the people here and ensure that all future travelers would be spared from injury.
Next, he traveled south to Oṭṭaka,
journeyed throughout the Five Indias,
and entered the kingdom of Magadha.
I wear plain garments and hold an empty pitcher in my hand,
which I place within the vihāra.
He established the Tathāgata teachings,
styled himself the Buddha Viśuddha,
and commanded the kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, and others to serve him.
In pursuit of the unsurpassed, true, and correct Way,
he spent twenty-four years;
this was during the time of King Mu.
I returned to the Central Plains and sent an envoy into the Eastern Sea,
reaching the islands of Penglai, Fangzhang, and others.
Arriving at Fusang,
he briefly visited the abode of the Great Emperor to compile the ranks of the immortals and determine their respective standings.
Furthermore, more than two hundred years after the eight kings had passed,
during the era of Youshen (幽深演),
the year was the cyclical year Xinyou.
When the three rivers tremble and surge,
a king is about to perish;
such a time has encountered the "one hundred and sixth" calamity.
"He cannot be restrained by non-humans.
I shall go further west to convert the various kingdoms."
Next, he entered the Western Sea and arrived at the islands of Juku, Liulinqi, and others. There,

he summoned from the ten directions all the immortals and great beings (*mahāsattva*), as well as those earthly lords who had recently attained the Way and those wandering immortals who had not yet received their official appointments— those whose filial piety and loyalty were supreme and who had just recently completed their trials and transitions.
In this manner, more than eighty thousand individuals of such standing evaluated the relative weight of their merits and karmic deeds,

and were granted positions among the five grades of immortal officials, the twenty-seven ranks of immortal transcendents and supreme sages, and the deities of the mountains, rivers, and the Three Heavens.
In this manner, they were all appointed and promoted.
Furthermore, more than sixty years passed until the time of Emperor Huan.
In the first yin month of the Jiazi year,
I, Ling Yinxi, mounted that essence of the moon.
Descending from the kingdom of Central India, he entered the mouth of Queen Śuddhodanā and was conceived by her;
he was named Siddhārtha.
He then renounced the rank of crown prince.
He entered the mountains to cultivate the Way,
attained the Unsurpassed Way,
and was titled Buddha.
He first established the twelve letters of Siddham, which,
through various combinations and permutations, comprise more than thirty thousand words,
extensively expounding the scriptures and precepts.
He sought the unsurpassed Dharma and further destroyed the ninety-six kinds of heterodox paths,
doing so for seventy years.
He manifested nirvana for the people.
During the reign of King Xiang,
the year was Yiyou (the 35th year of the sexagenary cycle).
I returned to China to teach and transform gods and humans,
and thereupon conferred upon Kong Qiu the teachings of benevolence, righteousness, and other such principles.
Thereafter, during the sixty years of King Dan’s reign,
the kingdom was divided from the capital;
the king lacked virtue.
I immediately ascended to Mount Kunlun and flew up to the Purple Microcosm,
spreading my vital breath throughout the three realms.
I nourish and sustain all beings.
Thereafter, after more than four hundred and fifty years have passed,
I shall mount upon the Way-energy of natural radiance.
From the realm of true stillness, he flew into the Sulin kingdom within the Jade World of Westna;
there he was born into a royal house and manifested as a crown prince.
He left home to enter the path,
was named Māmanī,
and turned the Great Wheel of Dharma.
He preached the Dharma of the Sūtras, Vinaya, Samādhi, Prajñā, and so forth,
even extending to the three periods of time and the two schools of thought,
thereby teaching and transforming devas and humans.
Causing them to know the fundamental limit (mūlānta),
reaching upward to the realm of light and downward to the dark paths of rebirth.
All sentient beings are delivered by this after the mani-jewel.
As my years approach fifty-nine,
the metal element is about to flourish; thus,
my Dharma shall surely prosper.
The sacred elephant of the West naturally adorns itself with colorful robes;
its arrival here in the Middle Continent is a manifestation of this very efficacy.
At this time, the yellow and white vapors merged,
and the three teachings were harmonized as one.
All return to me;
the benevolent shrines and monasteries join their ridgepoles and connect their eaves.
After the performance of this ritual for the Most Holy and Greatly Enlightened Honored One,
the Daoist masters of the Central Continent extensively explained the causes and conditions.
Acting as a vessel for the world,
he extensively propagated the Dharma; all sentient beings,
whether moving or stationary, were encompassed within it.
Universally saving and delivering all.
This is called the Dharma-gate that Comprehensively Encompasses All Dharmas.
*Laozi Huahu Jing*, Scroll Ten.

In the tenth fascicle, the tenth [chapter]: When I went to convert the Hu in the past, my head bore the "Heaven-Penetrating" crown, and my golden-purple robes illuminated the void with a brilliant, shimmering radiance.
The Hu King’s mind was stubborn and perverse; he would not honor me as his teacher. I then manifested the power of supernatural transformations.
In sum, he manifested divine majesty:
he commanded the sun to flee eastward and caused Mount Sumeru to collapse to the west.
Trampling upon the bridge of the *Gandharva* gods,
the sun and moon revolve to his left and right;
heaven and earth are alternately bright and dark.
The stars and constellations run astray;
various calamities arise everywhere in competition.
Even a skilled physician knows nothing of it.
The Hu king was struck with fear;
with palms joined toward me, he wept.
I bestowed upon him a teaching of great compassion.
The transformation gradually becomes subtle;
she discards her hairpin and forgoes one meal;
she leaves the upper robe off her right shoulder.
The men are called upāsakas and the women are called upāsikās;
those who converted Hu have now submitted.
Wandering his spirit through the Purple Microcosm,
when I was in Śrāvastī,
I issued these instructions to the body of Gautama.
Together with the Mahāsattva,
you brought the scriptural teachings to Eastern Qin,
spreading them throughout the realms of the Divine Land.
Reaching as far as the Eastern Sea,
he widely proclaimed the Dharma of the Most Honored One and instructed the deaf and worldly folk.
I shall bestow upon you the majestic and numinous Dharma;
may your transformative teachings fill a thousand years.
At the end of that time, you shall return.
Be careful not to harbor lingering attachment to Central Qin;
this will cause the Heavenly Majesty to grow wrathful,
and the Supreme One to stamp the earth in anger.
The temple collapsed and crumbled;
the dragon king licked the sacred scriptures.
There were eighty-four thousand disciples.
At one time, they received great conditions;
revolving through the five paths, not ten thousand out of ten thousand ascend to immortality.
I dwell above the Three Heavens.
Tears flow incessantly as he pities his son;
he reflects on the path his son has traveled and cannot turn back the conditions of death.
One cannot soar through the void,
nor can one bind oneself to enter the Yellow Springs;
the gates of heaven and the portals of earth are all blocked.
Once gone, there can be no returning.
Although you have succeeded in preserving the ancestral line,
it causes your son constant distress of heart.
If one opposes Heaven and violates the principles of the Earth,
calamities and punishments will befall one's own person;
yet the spirit has the power to alter both life and death.
Because the son's conduct was not true,
the thirty-six heavenly paths ultimately return to formlessness.
When I went to transform the West,
I ascended Mount Hua;
raising my eyes, I gazed upon Kunlun.
Mount Sumeru is clearly visible, suspended in space;
spreading my wings, I tread upon the pure void.
In an instant, I have reached the western heavens.
I saw only the Queen Mother of the West,
her solemn carriage about to turn eastward;
tens of thousands of jade maidens accompanied her.
His appearance was exceedingly beautiful and elegant;
his natural bearing was peerlessly dignified and majestic.
He held the Imperial Spirit Scripture with both hands.
Reciting the scriptures of the immortals,
you nourished my peerless beauty and led me into the celestial court.
The August Elder sat facing east,
his body radiant and pure;
he bestowed upon me the Way of the Immortal Sages.
I received and transformed the worthy ones of the world.
In the past, when I went west to convert others,
I ascended Mount Hua.
Looking northward toward Xuánmíng,
the Qín River flows vast and level;
there are few Han people, while the various other ethnic groups abound.
They will not believe in the True Words.
After more than a thousand years from now,
white bones will rise like hills and mountains.
Bodies lie upon the roads and in the wilds;
flowing blood forms vast, surging pools.
The Abyss could not bear to look upon her son.
Because of suffering, he became the Great Qin;
he chanted twenty laments of sorrowful sighs to demonstrate his penetration through the head.
The worthy one perceives the opportune moment for his descent;
the world does not encounter suffering or bitterness.
In the past, when I converted the barbarians, [I acted thus].
He ascended Mount Taibai in the west and cultivated his person among the rocky crags;
from the four directions, the various immortals gathered there.
The jade maidens carried the whey and curd;
the immortals sang the scriptural texts;
the devas and nāgas followed and escorted from behind.
The White Tiger gallops with severed heads from his mouth;
the Dark Warrior (Xuanwu) carries bells and drums upon his back;
the Vermilion Bird (Zhuque) holds banners and streamers.
He transformed the Hu and attained the Buddha-way;
his sixteen-foot adamantine body then bestowed the oral teachings upon him.
The subsequent scriptural text shall be preserved hereafter.
After I have ascended to the Nine Heavens,
you must carve wood to fashion my likeness.
In the past, when I departed from the Zhou dynasty,
I traveled westward toward Kaśmīra;
my route led me through the Hangu Pass.
He met the person of Yin Xi in person.
Yin Xi had penetrated the profound and mysterious;
observing the heavens, he beheld purple clouds.
Knowing that I was about to pass westward,
he bathed and observed the fasts,
maintaining the incense and lamps day and night.
He instructed the gatekeeper to receive me with a tablet of introduction and invited me to enter the imperial court.
They strike and beat me countless times,
seeking to take [me] from my body;
yet the Way takes a person’s sincerity and faith.
For three days he did not speak;
I knew that his joyful heart had reached its peak.
He left behind the *Wuxian wen* (Five Thousand Words on Joy).
Desiring to seek longevity,
one reads this to refine the spirit; soon,
with joy, one shall enter the Western Regions.
Qianxi has been promoted to the rank of True Person.
When I transformed the Hu in the past,
there was no part of heaven I did not traverse.
Heaven’s canopy overspreads the six realms;
my body has endured every hardship.
The Hu people do not recognize the Dharma.
Though they set fire to my body,
my body remained unharmed;
then again, they cast me into a deep abyss.
The Dragon King has severed the flow of the water veins;
it no longer circulates.
Fools all lament with sorrow.
I have wronged this worthy person’s life.
I shall summon the power of surging waves to raise him up and place him in the heavens.
The sun and moon were bright above his head,
their light illuminating hundreds of millions;
only then did the heart of the Hu King awaken.
Knowing that I am a sage,
he bowed his head and sought to repent for his transgressions,
saying, "I now wish to serve you, my lord."
I humbly pray that you descend with your numinous spirit to bring life and vitality to the people of this land;
I regard my enemies as my own infants.
Disregarding enmity and suspicion,
he transformed the men of his age;
whether sitting or reclining, they recited the scriptural texts.
My body was without the adornment of worldly splendor,
yet in the end I attained rebirth in heaven;
thus I inform the people of this age.
Among the worthy ones within the three realms,
those who seek the path of long life must not cherish this body worth a thousand pieces of gold.
Having emerged from the ground of death,
one returns to obtain the conditions for life;
a lotus flower grows amidst the flames.
You are indeed the Most True One;
do not harbor thoughts of birth or death.
Having attained the Way, you shall ascend to the Pure Heavens.
Before I was burdened, I possessed true faith;
I lost my son and my body worth a thousand pieces of gold.
When I formerly studied the Way, I...
Ascending the cliffs and traversing the long pines,
I wind my way through the secluded valleys in search of the Holy Sage.
By consuming the Nirvana Powder,
he gradually attained the state of immortality within his nine-layered chamber.
I beheld the Immortal Youth,
his body exquisitely magnificent,
peerless within the two realms of heaven and earth.
He bestowed upon me the medicine of primordial qi;
suddenly, my celestial sagacity was awakened.
Five Poems of Sorrowful Lament by Yin Xi. Five Poems of Sorrowful Lament by Yin Xi. Yin Xi addresses the people of the world.
If you seek the path of long life,
do not seek the glory of this world.
When I attained the Way in the past, [I did so in this manner].
As the Lord of the Pass,
he bestows rewards three times each day,
with various silks and gold and silver.
Not considering it as one's own possession,
he bestowed it upon the poor; by day,
he was occupied with the affairs of the king.
At night he practiced the arts of the immortal seers;
by consuming pine and bitter cypress,
his fragile life was thereby sustained.
With sincere devotion, the divine spirits grant protection;
guarding the truth, one looks up to the azure heavens.
Thus, one attains the Way of Heaven and Earth.
I encountered the body of the Old Lord,
who rebuked me for my parents,
yet left behind the Five Thousand Words.
I read it in secret for three years, transforming my spirit;
he then bestowed upon me the prescriptions of the immortal sages.
The entire substance is naturally understood.
In the past, I ascended to the Nine Heavens and looked down toward the profound darkness.
One sees only soaring transcendents,
their aligned wings casting shadows that clarify the heavens;
they pay court to the Lord of the Nine Heavens at dawn.
The Most High August Lord cleansed his six internal organs within;
he received and studied the texts of the immortals and sages.
Wang Qiao attained the holy Way and traveled among the Five Peaks;
he ingested qi and consumed the essence of jade.
His life span is equal to that of Heaven.
In the past, when he was practicing the Way, he ascended a mountain and traversed its high peaks; as he moved along, he beheld valleys a hundred *zhang* deep.
The brilliant and vast realm is long;
it possesses the infinite divine pneuma (*śakti*).
How does one reach the Western Land?
Originally intending to cross the Red Valley,
he shed thousands of lines of tears,
reflecting that his own past transgressions were heavy.
Fifth, his inner heart was shattered:
"In the past, when I sought the Way,
I traversed thousands of cliffs."
Wandering beyond the eight wildernesses,
barefoot and without clothing,
he traveled east across the realm where the sun rises.
On the clear mountains of Xixin,
my feet tread heavily upon the earth;
in my hand, I grasp the Lesser Star.
On the way, he encountered the Queen Mother of the West,
who asked him, "Where has my son gone?
He is ashamed that his person does not study the Way."
I desired to seek out an immortal master;
moved by my utmost sincerity,
he begged me for my shoes and my robe.
Only then can one learn the Way;
the immortal breath gradually becomes subtle and faint.
My parents marvel at my lateness.
Wailing and weeping day and night;
the Great Way is contrary to the mundane.
Once gone, there is no returning.
My lofty aspirations grow ever more distant;
I am unaware that my heart and liver are being crushed.
Though I have attained the Way of immortality, [I remain thus].
His physical strength was exceedingly feeble,
yet his mental vigor never regressed;
he has now become the Teacher of Gods and Humans.
In the past, when he went forth to study the Way,
his traces were likewise difficult to find;
he traveled eastward to the realm where the sun rises.
The trees are lush and deep;
I have reached Jambudvīpa in the south.
Great fires consume my body.
Going west, one arrives at Kujūni;
there one sees only golden city gates and blue dragons guarding the city walls.
The White Tiger guards before the city;
the golden palaces pierce the heavens.
The Most High dwells there in profound stillness.
The radiance of light and shadow illuminates the void;
the immortals are of peerless majesty and beauty,
all holding yellow scrolls in their hands.
Reciting the Scripture of Longevity,
he faces north and enters the profound darkness;
the great waters are vast and deep.
He circumambulated the heavens several hundred times;
as his soles pressed down heavily upon them,
he was born anew and thereby attained the Way of the Immortals.
He grasped the spirits of heaven and earth;
his son was able to expound my Way,
and by day he ascended to heaven.
The Seven Lamentations of the Supreme August Lord Lao; the Mistress of the Thirty-Six Palaces, the Supreme August Lord Lao.
Out of compassion for those in the world below,
you have bestowed your divine teachings upon the sages of this age.
You, my son, wish to cultivate merit for the afterlife.
First, one should realize the profound stillness;
though one may attain nobility at birth,
it is not equal to the glory of the past.
The immortal mounts his dragon chariot to welcome you on a journey through the pure heavens,
ascending to the golden pavilions and halls above.
He sits and lies within the void;
when he walks, flying immortals follow him;
his majestic deportment reaches up to the heavens.
Ascending to the eastern head of heaven at dawn,
arriving at the western edge of heaven by dusk,
they sport and delight beyond the nine heavens.
He acts with unrestrained freedom in his extensive dealings;
he drives and employs a hundred ghosts and presides over ten thousand pieces of gold.
I pity the ignorant people of this world;
they do not believe in the deities within the unseen realm,
yet relying on their own strength, they harm the virtuous and good.
He does not avoid those of virtuous conduct;
he gallops his horse to the east and west,
imagining himself to be always without rival.
Good and evil all have their retribution;
though the karmic conditions may arise in a mere instant,
the divine spirits above behold them.
He dispatches a messenger to go directly and drag [the offender] away;
from the head down to the soles of the feet,
he is bound and cast into the gate of the Celestial Prison.
The five poisons aggravate one another;
malevolent spirits come to strike and invade;
though the mouth attempts to chant, words cannot be spoken.
The wife called out to the god Cangtian:
"Do not resent that the deity does not grant protection;
it is because your conduct lacks benevolence."
I lament those of this age who do not believe in the divine and the spiritual;
their ancestors have already planted seeds of merit for them.
May descendants tread this path;
may their clothing be warm and their food sufficient;
may calamities and punishments not reach their doors.
With his breath he sighs toward the heavens,
claiming that he has been thus all day long;
yet when one looks at the Master, he appears profoundly remote and vast.
When one falls ill and prostrates oneself in supplication,
though outwardly respectful, the heart lacks reverence;
the divine spirits know the person within.
The three *hún* spirits are bound to hell;
the seven *pò* spirits hang suspended in heaven.
The three *hún* dissipate and vanish.
The five spirits are not at peace;
they await the arrival of the Lord of Death to seize and carry them away.
The Prime Minister treads upon the ground in anger.
If the deity on the left does not eliminate death,
and the deity on the right does not establish life,
the life-deity will not provide protection.
The deity of death enters the body;
one may suffer from pain in the waist and back,
or suffer from pain in the head and eyes.
The hundred vessels no longer flow;
in an instant one enters the Yellow Spring. The gates of heaven and earth are closed; once gone, there is no returning.
I pity the foolish people of this world.
One who does not believe in the deities of the afterlife and fails to show reverence while alive must repay the causes of their transgressions once dead.
The official in charge pursues from behind as they are driven northward,
running east and west;
they embrace the sands to fill the rivers and seas.
Carrying stones, they pile up high mountains;
by day they cannot eat,
and by night they cannot sleep.
In the morning he was given one hundred blows with a staff;
in the evening he was given one thousand lashes with a whip.
Unable to endure the agony of such interrogation, he [confessed].
They sell their sins to the living;
two by two they drag each other along,
until finally death brings about the extinction of their entire lineage.
All this results from a lack of reverence for the Way.
The divine spirits examine and scrutinize human beings;
why, then, do you not revere the True Deity?
Through birth and death, one attains ascent to heaven;
there is glory in life and joy for the deceased.
Through birth and death, one receives and is graced by the Buddha's benevolence.
I pity the people of this age;
they do not believe in the spirits within the unseen realm.
Within a single household, there may be ten children.
Even if one acts with unrestrained cruelty,
the divine spirit observes all without exception;
it will never unjustly take a person's life.
Some were young women with exquisite features;
others were wonderful youths.
The gates collapsed and the doors fell into ruin.
Students are like floating clouds;
even in death, they do not escape the passage of years.
Their lamentations and weeping continue to follow one another.
Wife and children have sunk into oblivion;
I alone remain solitary.
I call out to Heaven, but it is dark and remote.
Crying out, "The earth is also deep," they were unable to reproach themselves;
each instead blamed their venerable teacher.
Though I wish to contemplate the path of goodness,
my ten sons will not return;
I thus inform the people of this age.
One should practice the Way with earnest diligence;
for kindness does not arise in vain,
and the divine spirits will surely repay it to the person.
In the past, there was Liu Zhongbo,
who was single-mindedly devoted to the Way;
he exhorted the wicked to follow what is good.
Each year they assemble a multitude of sages;
with incense and lamps, they are diligent day and night.
Thus they are also able to move the Lord of Heaven.
When life is exhausted, one must die;
the various deities and the manifest heavens—
the three souls fly away and dissolve.
When the seven *po* spirits enter the star of death,
the deity on the right erases the name from the register of death,
and the deity on the left inscribes it upon the register of life.
When the Lord of Death arrives, he brings ultimate salvation;
the Left Minister, treading upon the ground in wrath,
proclaims throughout the twenty hells.
The spirit emerges from the body of Zhongbo;
the three souls return and flow again,
and the seven po-ghosts return and enter the body.
The blood vessels circulate once more,
the hundred joints become firm again,
and the face and features grow even more dignified and handsome.
The flesh and bones became even more distinct;
after lying dead for twenty-one days,
the corpse was laid down and he was restored to life once more.
I tell the people of this age:
they cannot distinguish true from false by mere bones;
they do not speak with one another when at leisure.
The messenger of death arrives in haste seeking people;
the dead are like flowing water,
and those who depart are like drifting clouds.
In the Qin River valley, the army and horses are pure;
in the central courtyard, thickets of brambles grow.
Not even one out of a hundred remains.
Reflect upon my original words:
why not study the Way of the Immortals?
Then the human body may be preserved forever.
The Verses on the Lord Lao’s Sixteen Transformations: In the first transformation, he was born in the south, appearing like fire.
Emerging from the womb and falling to the ground, he was able to sit alone.
With lips joined, I recited the sutras with a faint and feeble voice;
tears fell from my eyes like rolling pearls.
My parents were struck with wonder and alarm at me in this world.
Furthermore, fearing the cold and frost, I came to bear fruit;
though my body is clothed in celestial garments, who would recognize me?
This was during the second transformation.
Born in the Western Peak region of Hanchuan,
he was raised in a royal household where he refined his spirit.
Upon emerging from the womb and touching the ground, he was already able to speak.
Brilliantly shining like gold and silver,
with thirty-six colors of exquisite silken patterns;
the king, filled with joy, assembled his ministers.
A refined and elegant scholar of noble character suddenly undergoes a transformation and becomes a Great Man;
his hair and eyebrows turn white, and his head supports the heavens.
At the time of the third transformation,
his form changed and his substance was altered as he was in the north;
upon emerging from the womb and falling to the ground, he was already able to sit upon a couch.
The voices of those chanting the sutras together ring out clearly;
upon his forehead are the three marks and twelve lines,
and his two hands remain open, holding no worldly writings.
Its names correspond to Heaven and Earth; its thickness matches Yin and Yang.
From stone it enters metal, soaring with ease.
At the time of the fourth transformation.
Born in the east with a body the color of blue-green jade,
he was able to pound grain as soon as he emerged from the womb and fell to the ground;
with his mouth closed, he recited the sutras in a harmonious and resonant voice.
By day she is borne by her mother; by night she rides the dragon.
Upon Mount Kunlun, she moves now west, now east.
She ascends to heaven, enters the earth, and mounts the void.
The rishi was attended by tens of thousands of followers.
At that time, his spiritual essence was in communication with the divine.
This occurred during the fifth transformation.
Born in the Middle Capital at Luochuan,
he practiced meritorious deeds for one hundred thousand years atop the peaks and summits of Mount Song and Shaoshi.
He instructed tens of thousands of celestial immortals.
Equally attaining ascent to heaven and entry into the azure clouds,
you looked down upon the Zhou dynasty for eight hundred years;
when the mandate ended and the numbers were exhausted, you departed for Kapiśī.
Having converted the Hu and attained Buddhahood, he returned to Eastern Qin,
where he propagated the Way of the Teachings and perfected the Celestial Writings.
At the time of the sixth transformation:
Born upon the dry land in the northwest corner,
he mapped out heaven and earth and established the Five Peaks;
he arranged the constellations and charted the Four Great Rivers.
The twenty-eight lunar mansions are assigned to the local districts;
the sun and moon shine brightly as the sovereigns of the lower realms.
Moving like flowing water, they complete their circuit.
The wise observe this and know its urgency:
when rain falls at the proper time, the five grains ripen;
ten thousand people eat them, and their great transformation is sufficient.
At the time of the seventh transformation,
he was born in the north at the edge of the ocean;
upon emerging from the womb and falling to the ground, his voice resounded profoundly.
Delighting in song and dance, free from sorrow,
she creates music and plays the *konghou* lute;
when the ten thousand lords come to invite her, she uses it to dispel their grief.
The Yellow River serves as the path to the end of one’s journey;
traversing the world alone, one travels with joyful ease.
At the time of the eighth transformation, one is born in the northeast, in the region of Gen.
The diagrams depict heaven and earth; I follow their sequence.
The lay practitioner Vimalakīrti, wishing to engage in seated meditation, must be well-versed in the vital energies.
The scriptures are thoroughly understood and there are śarīras;
seeing my marks and signs, you must believe and aspire with longing.
Moved by your singular sincerity, I did not wait for others in succession.
Attaining equality, they ascend to heaven and do not fall to earth.
At the time of the ninth transformation,
they descend to the Yellow Springs and rectify the pillars of the earth.
When heaven and earth were first opened, the Gate of Earth was established;
the four seasonal energies were not yet of Yang, abiding in the realm of darkness.
Although there were people, they were unable to speak.
When I entered the body, I bestowed myself upon the six viscera:
the ribs served as lateral passages and the heart was the sovereign.
From that time onward, I have been able to speak.
There is a sequential order among the noble and the humble, the great and the small;
the myriad heavens acclaim the Transmission of the Way as their father.
At the time of the ten transformations—
Born in the southeast, he emerges from the Gate of Wind;
he paints forth the heavenly paths and establishes the mountains and rivers.
He sets up the Five Peaks and gathers the immortal spirits therein.
Breathing forth cold and heat, it gives birth to the myriad people; it dispels the vexed qi of sentient beings so that humans may attain the Real.
It establishes the five viscera and bestows them upon the spirit and mind;
it moves the six spirits and enables speech.
Birth and death occur in the space of a moment;
like water flowing eastward, when will it ever return?
Meeting by chance, they succeed one another without pause.
Why not practice the good and seek long life?
Wandering aimlessly through worldly customs, one enters a sticky trap;
unable to escape, one suffers the loss of one's own body.
Seeking to transcend the world through meditative absorption therein,
yet failing to firmly restrain the mind, the roots of the sage remain unsteady;
like those who are blind, deaf, or mute, their teachings are inconsistent.
Because in his previous life the son slandered the sutras and the treatise,
and the Daoist reviled the sages;
as he was in evil, he must receive retribution for the conditions of his transgressions.
Simply exert yourself in self-reproach and do not resent Heaven.
At the time of the eleventh transformation,
you were born in the southern continent of Jambudvīpa.
He fashioned heaven and earth, creating the conditioned;
he brought forth the myriad things through the infant.
Yin and yang face one another, following each other in mutual succession.
Sentient beings, having received their vital breath, each act for themselves;
their offspring multiply in great numbers, filling the earth and the ponds.
They seek their livelihood by guarding their fields, yet find no rest in their labors.
The kalpas were exhausted and all at once diminished;
floods surged to the heavens reaching as far as Mozhī.
The seeds of the people were selected and preserved for Fuxi.
Contemplating and reflecting upon this, one establishes the *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas;
only the Great Sage and [the practitioner] know each other.
At the time of the twelve transformations.
Born in the southwest at twilight,
people loathe and despise this aged body;
through skillful means and strategic methods, one receives a new one.
Entrusting himself to a womb and taking on the form of a mundane python,
he recited the sutras within the womb without encountering anyone;
he emerged from the left flank, not by way of the birth canal.
He fell to the ground and took seven steps amidst the filth;
nine dragons bathed him while no one heard.
The king rejoiced and established him in the Eastern Palace.
He took as his new wife the woman named Qiuyi;
eight hundred female musicians provided entertainment for him,
yet he remained undisturbed in his dhyāna for eighty-four bushels [of time].
He emptied his treasury and gave it to the poor.
Eighteen people on the road went to the palace gate.
A merchant acted as a most hideous Brahmin.
"I ask, when will the Prince return?
His silence has moved the King's heart;
his riding of the King's white elephant has provoked the King's wrath."
Master Huáng, knowing his intent, did not speak with him.
Fǎzhù remained at Mount Tánṭè,
casting himself before a starving tiger to seek the gateway of the Way.
He manifested as hundreds of white dogs;
he piled up his bones like Mount Sumeru to show future generations.
He transmitted this message to later students: "One must be diligent."
Do not covet that which is foul and disgraceful, for it will ruin your life;
you shall sink into the six realms of existence, where rebirth is difficult to achieve.
Do not disbelieve my words; you shall see the truth when the time comes.
At the time of the thirteenth transformation,
he transformed his form and changed his body in Kaśmīra;
descending from heaven, he was without root and without foundation.
He was titled the Vajra-body of Maitreya;
the Hu people, failing to recognize him, raised up a false deity,
mobilized their armies and masses, and surrounded the Sage.
In the country of Jixin, to the north, the Old Lord was burned.
The Most High, out of compassion and pity for sentient beings,
gradually led them forward by preaching the Dharma wheel.
Having shaved off his beard and hair to become a practitioner of the Way,
he crosswise donned a collarless *nirvāṇa-saṃghāṭī*;
with his head covered and a collar worn, he awaits the Lord of Old.
Holding his *khakkhara* staff, he startled the insects in the ground;
lying down, he would contemplate the deities, and rising, he would recite the sutras.
His breath became disordered, and he desired to go to the East (Dong) and Qin.
The dream was fulfilled when Emperor Ming sent Zhang Qian to welcome [the scriptures];
a white elephant carried the sutras to the city of Luoyang.
The House of Han established a crown prince devoid of human feeling.
Having abandoned home, parents, and worldly habits to practice as a śramaṇa,
he lacked a sincere heart even when fleeing from soldiers;
he did not cultivate the Dharma, but lived in poverty to earn a livelihood.
Grasping at the mind without firmness leads back to the entanglements of secular life;
eighty-four thousand karmic conditions for retribution arise.
They destroy stupas and desecrate temples, slaughtering practitioners of the Way.
They smashed the bronze statues to extract the gold;
before they had even flourished for long, they were replaced by new ones.
Although these have been preserved, the Emperor remains fearful in his heart.
At the time of the fourteenth transformation,
he transformed his body and altered his appearance within the city of Jinwei;
there, the śramaṇas surrounded the city as he preached the sūtra verses.
When it came time for the most grievous sinners to be saved,
the Hu people heard of this and were struck with fear and wonder;
they arrived in great throngs to pay their respects.
He prostrated himself with his head to the ground, repenting his transgressions and seeking to receive the precepts;
he vowed never to retreat, even to the point of carving his flesh and piercing his bones,
burning his fingers and training his arms as a self-consecrated oath.
A man who does not take a wife but sits in contemplative meditation will,
after death, become a corpse at Śītavana to be devoured by hawks and hawks;
his spirit shall be transferred to nirvāṇa, O Śāriputra.
His bones were obtained in eight *hu* and distributed throughout various kingdoms.
In this way, one may transcend and depart from afflictions and desires;
by subjecting the body to hardship in pursuit of the Way, [enlightenment] can be attained immediately.
During the fifteenth transformation,
he traveled westward to teach and convert the people of Jibin;
after the various regions of the Hu lands had been harmonized, he returned to Kāśī.
Violating the borders, plundering and consuming, you buy and raise people;
as a man, you guard the passes, yet you are an upāsikā.
When I enter the kingdom, I shall compose skillful words.
He preached the transformation of a man who received the Three Refuges;
gradually inducing him forward, he taught the Wheel of Dharma,
shaved his beard and hair, and made him a practitioner of the Way.
The male is the Upādhyāya and the female is the Ācāryā;
they assume the roles of parents to ordain monks and nuns.
When teacher and disciple ordain one another, the principle is free from partiality.
The spirit has ascended to Nirvana and returned to the Purple Microcosm;
the Four Guardians are peaceful and harmonious, bringing peace to our spirits.
The Hu people, filled with longing, sigh and weep.
Cast a golden image in my likeness;
enter and prostrate at the three times of day seeking long life.
You must not enter where it is utterly silent and desolate.
Bowing his head, he gazes at the ground and looks up at the heavens, wondering when the Great Sage, the Truly Authentic One, will return.
At the time of the sixteenth transformation,
he was born in the Reed Grove, named Yaśas.
The great wealthy elder Jyotiṣka had a hand-towel that resembled a dragon or snake;
he sent a wind to blow it away until it reached the royal palace.
The king, having obtained it, sighed with great amazement;
he raised an army and mobilized his hosts to come toward the house.
A hundred *li* from the dwelling, he saw a lotus flower.
In the kingdom, there was one who had been under observation for a month;
the king’s mind grew malicious toward him, and he desired to destroy his family.
Suddenly, [the house] transformed into a pure white dwelling.
Leaving home to seek the Way, he was named Śākyamuni.
In the five-hundredth year [after his parinirvāṇa],
riding upon dragons and driving tigers, the Way shall flourish.
The records of the vast land of Han are long;
thirty-six men, counted as brothers,
traversed the road to the Northern Gate and soared like clouds in mid-air.
Fresh Lu wine was brought out and we went together to taste it;
by the side of Mount Emei, we made *xi-chang* (fine wine).
At this moment, our joy knows no end.
The lifespan of those born in the Īṣādhāra heaven is long;
at six hundred years,
one world passes away and another world returns.
The city walls remain as they were, yet the people are no more;
though many gaze upon them, who among them knows me?
Life and death differ from one another, bringing sorrow to all.
Why not study the Way while worldly desires wane?
Who is it that hesitates to the northwest and sighs deeply?
It is Yieyue who delights in life and governs the Taiwei Palace.
The Scripture of Laozi’s Conversion of the Barbarians, Scroll Ten, from the Canon of Jingtu Monastery.
